Bright Electricals, an establishment dealing in household electrical goods and fittings situated in the same general vicinity as certain other complaints already on file with this office, that he too has been approached on a recurring basis by an individual identified as Rakesh Pawar demanding periodic payment, failing which vague but unmistakably threatening remarks were made regarding the continued smooth operation of the complainant's business. The complainant states that on one recent occasion, rather than handing over cash as had been the practice on prior visits, he was instead instructed to transfer the demanded amount to a bank account, being provided with a set of details sufficient to identify the account only by its last four digits, namely an account ending in the digits 7743, this being, as far as the complainant is aware, intended as a "cleaner" alternative to the usual cash handover, a characterization he recalls Pawar himself using in the course of explaining the new arrangement. The complainant further states that he complied with this instruction on the one occasion in question, at approximately 12:15 hrs, out of fear of the consequences of non-compliance, but has since approached this thana upon learning, through conversation with other affected shopkeepers in the area, that a formal investigation into the broader arrangement is already underway. The complainant additionally recalls that Pawar, while explaining the new payment arrangement, mentioned that "everyone would be moving to this method eventually," a remark the complainant did not fully understand at the time but which he now considers significant in light of learning that other shopkeepers have made similar complaints. The complainant further states that he has retained no written record of the account details provided to him at the time, having entered them directly into his banking application and subsequently deleted the message by which they were conveyed, out of an abundance of caution regarding his own safety, though he believes the transaction itself would remain reflected in his bank's own records and has accordingly consented to those records being obtained by the investigating officer. FIR No. 0529/2026

Anand Sweets, a long-established sweet shop in the locality patronized by residents of the surrounding area, that he too has been subjected to periodic demands for payment of a sum of money, the individual making such demands on his premises being one Rakesh Pawar, who is stated to arrive on his rounds, on occasion accompanied by a driver, in a vehicle bearing registration MH04XY2345, which the complainant has observed parked outside his shop on more than one occasion during the course of such visits, on one occasion for a period sufficient for the complainant to note down the registration out of an abundance of caution, though he did not, at the relevant time, report the matter for fear of reprisal. The complainant states that the amounts demanded have varied somewhat from visit to visit, and that his own recollection of the precise sums involved may differ slightly from that of neighbouring shopkeepers who have, he understands, been subjected to similar demands, this variance being attributed by the complainant to the passage of time and the informal, undocumented nature of the transactions in question rather than to any deliberate inconsistency on the part of the collector. It is further stated that the complainant has, on occasion, overheard Pawar referring during phone conversations conducted within earshot to a person addressed only as "Bhai," without any further particulars being audible to the complainant, one such conversation being recalled by the complainant as having taken place at around 17:45 hrs on a weekday evening, during which Pawar was heard to say only a few words before stepping further away, out of earshot, to continue the call. The complainant additionally states that he has, on the advice of a relative, begun maintaining a private note of the dates on which such visits occur, though he acknowledges that this record is neither comprehensive nor entirely precise, having been started only after several months of the arrangement having already been in place, and that he is willing to make this note available to the investigating officer should it prove of any assistance to the present enquiry. FIR No. 0512/2026

Metro Mobile Repair, a small establishment dealing in the repair and servicing of mobile telephones situated in a different market area of the city, that he has similarly been subjected to periodic demands for payment, in his case at the hands of an individual identified as one Salim Sheikh, who is stated to visit the complainant's shop at irregular but recurring intervals, on occasion accompanied by a second, unidentified individual who does not himself speak but remains present during the course of the visit, apparently for the purpose of lending an air of seriousness to the demand being made. The complainant states that payments have, on more than one occasion, been made not in cash but through a digital transfer arranged, as he understood it from remarks made by Sheikh himself, "through the account," the complainant having been provided on one such occasion with a set of digits corresponding to a bank account ending in a particular four-digit sequence, though he did not retain a written record of the same and could not, at the time of recording this statement, recall the precise figures involved. It is further stated that Sheikh, on at least one occasion, made passing reference to "the man who runs all this," without providing any further detail, the complainant forming the impression that Sheikh himself was not the ultimate beneficiary of the payments being extracted from him but rather an intermediary acting on behalf of some further, unnamed individual. The complainant recalls that on the most recent such visit, which he places at approximately 18:30 hrs in the evening, Sheikh appeared somewhat more hurried than on prior occasions, checking his phone twice during the brief exchange and remarking, seemingly to himself, that he was "running late for the other side." FIR No. 0507/2026

Iqbal Ansari, who is alleged to be the central coordinator of the extortion racket under investigation, understood to direct and oversee the activities of both Rakesh Pawar and Salim Sheikh, the two field-level collectors operating in separate localities within the city, without himself directly approaching or collecting from any of the shopkeepers concerned, this division of roles being consistent with information already gathered from multiple complainants across the several related matters presently under investigation. The preliminary remarks of the investigating officer note that the identification of a named individual behind the moniker previously used represents a significant step forward in the investigation, and that steps are accordingly being taken to place the said individual under closer observation, commencing from approximately 06:00 hrs on the following morning, with a view to gathering further corroborative material sufficient to support formal proceedings against him. It is further remarked that this development, taken together with the several related complaints already on file naming Pawar and Sheikh as field-level collectors, is expected to materially assist in establishing the complete structure of the network under investigation, including the precise manner in which instructions and funds are understood to flow between the individual now named and the two collectors operating in their respective localities. This office additionally notes that the present development has prompted a review of all related complaints filed to date, with a view to identifying any further shopkeepers who may not yet have come forward but who may nonetheless have been subjected to similar demands, a canvassing exercise expected to be carried out over the coming weeks in coordination with local shopkeeper associations in the affected market areas. FIR No. 0518/2026

Iqbal Ansari as the central coordinator of the extortion network under investigation, it being noted in the present narrative that the said Iqbal Ansari has, on more than one occasion recorded through independent means, been found to be in direct telephonic contact with both Rakesh Pawar and Salim Sheikh within short intervals of one another, the content of such calls, to the extent ascertainable, relating to the collection of amounts from specific shopkeepers already known to this office through related complaints, including reference on more than one occasion to establishments by name. It is further stated that this pattern of direct contact with both collectors, now recorded on more than one separate occasion, is considered by the investigating officer to establish, with a reasonable degree of confidence, that the individual named in earlier proceedings functions as the coordinating link between what would otherwise appear to be two independent collection operations, rather than the two collectors operating entirely independently of one another as might otherwise be inferred from the geographic separation of their respective areas of activity. The most recent such instance of corroborated contact is noted to have occurred during the early evening hours, at approximately 19:00 hrs, consistent with the general pattern of timing already observed in connection with earlier intercepted calls forming part of this investigation. This office further notes that the pattern of contact observed to date, taken together with the statements already recorded from several affected shopkeepers, is considered sufficient at this stage to justify continued and intensified surveillance of the individual concerned, with a formal request for judicial authorization of extended technical surveillance measures being prepared separately for submission through the appropriate channel. It is additionally remarked that the present finding, when read alongside the account of direct instruction earlier recorded in connection with the identification of the individual concerned, is considered by this office to substantially close the evidentiary gap that had previously existed between the observational surveillance conducted in the field and the technical evidence gathered through call-detail analysis. FIR No. 0540/2026
